liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Terrapin Station** (3 reviews): The jam following Terrapin is heard as a Mind Left Body jam; Jerry seems to lose track of being onstage during Terrapin, though the jam afterward is cool [23][25][26]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet is called one of the raunchiest versions, played in serious overdrive; Jerry's Scarlet lead runs about 4:30 with four or five crescendos, unlike other 1985 versions [27][31]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): The Scarlet into Bucket transition is described as interesting [25]
- **Spanish Jam** (1 review): A full-on Spanish Jam appears, giving an interesting picture of 1985 [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-03-22.148300.PandP.aud.damico.tobin.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 165 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording ran extremely fast, about one second per minute [1]
- **gd1985-03-22.163332.akg451.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 163 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd85-03-22.oade-schoeps.sacks.23144.sbeok.flacf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 169 min; rated 3.5/5 by 16 [5]. Said about its sound: Sound described as crisp; Smooth audience recording that conveys what a live 1985 show was like; Decent audience sound, slightly peaky on the loudest passages [27][28][29][30][31][32]
- **gd1985-03-22.148302.dts.tobin.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 165 min [6]
- **gd85-03-22.gibbs.hudson.13782.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 152 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [15]. Said about its sound: Slightly less distant and clearer in the highs; all recordings suffer from the venue's acoustics [33]

## Around the show

- Audience members clap along during Terrapin [28]
- Reviewer arrived hours before, made a sign, quickly got a ticket in the parking lot, and met Navy friends [30]
- Big video screens at the venue are viewed as marking a decline [32]
- Not as epic as the summer 1985 shows, though still worth hearing [23]
- Many better 1985 shows exist; this one lacks cohesion for much of its length [25]
- Second set is long for an 1985 show, and the first set is excellent [29]
- Judged better-sounding than the other audience recordings of this show [33]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-03-22.148300.PandP.aud.damico.tobin.flac16**: taped by Joe Damico; transferred by Patched and pitch corrected soundboard  (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: Patched and pitch corrected soundboard (44/16) [1]. Also: Mixed by an archive.org user; FLAC conversion made in November 2019; Patches cover the end of Terrapin Station and Black Peter [1]
- **gd1985-03-22.163332.akg451.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob, Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG 451's w/ CK8 shotguns (Left + Right) + (1)Neumann U87 (Center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [3]
- **gd85-03-22.oade-schoeps.sacks.23144.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Doug Oade - Darren Sacks; source: Oade Brothers Recording: Schoeps CMC441s (90deg, 17cm) > Oade M118 > Oade mod SONY PCM-F1 [5]. Also: Reviewer watches video of the second set synced with the Oade source; Transfer went from master PCM to DAW via Prodif, then to wav and FLAC [5][26]
- **gd1985-03-22.148302.dts.tobin.flac16**: transferred by DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix by Kevin Tobin; source: DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix [6]. Also: A DTS surround-sound mix on CD, made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in 2019 [6]
- **gd85-03-22.gibbs.hudson.13782.sbeok.shnf**: source: Taper:Mark Gibbs Nak 300's > Sony D5 > Master CASS > SoundMAX Digital Audio > CD Wav > SHN Transferred by John Hudson [15]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Brian Baumwoll Grateful Dead: [1985-03-21 Hampton Coliseum, Hampton, VA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1985-03-21-hampton-coliseum-hampton-va-usa/) [35]

claims.text: The jam following Terrapin is heard as a Mind Left Body jam
A full-on Spanish Jam appears, giving an interesting picture of 1985
Not as epic as the summer 1985 shows, though still worth hearing
Jerry seems to lose track of being onstage during Terrapin, though the jam afterward is cool
Many better 1985 shows exist; this one lacks cohesion for much of its length
The Scarlet into Bucket transition is described as interesting
Jerry forgets some lyrics but jams it out strongly at the end; video of set two exists
Reviewer watches video of the second set synced with the Oade source
Scarlet is called one of the raunchiest versions, played in serious overdrive
Sound described as crisp
Audience members clap along during Terrapin
Smooth audience recording that conveys what a live 1985 show was like
Decent audience sound, slightly peaky on the loudest passages
Second set is long for an 1985 show, and the first set is excellent
Reviewer arrived hours before, made a sign, quickly got a ticket in the parking lot, and met Navy friends
Considered one of the better audience recordings the reviewer has found
Jerry's Scarlet lead runs about 4:30 with four or five crescendos, unlike other 1985 versions
Audience noise makes the recording sound extra rowdy
Arena sound is oversaturated and muddled, with odd crowd reactions mid-song
Big video screens at the venue are viewed as marking a decline
Slightly less distant and clearer in the highs; all recordings suffer from the venue's acoustics
Judged better-sounding than the other audience recordings of this show
Mixed by an archive.org user; FLAC conversion made in November 2019
The recording ran extremely fast, about one second per minute
Patches cover the end of Terrapin Station and Black Peter
Recorded by Rob Eaton using AKG 451 and Neumann U87 microphones; Charlie Miller coordinated
Oade Brothers recorded with Schoeps CMC441s through an Oade M118 into a modified Sony PCM-F1
Transfer went from master PCM to DAW via Prodif, then to wav and FLAC
A DTS surround-sound mix on CD, made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in 2019
